content: Acute muscle soreness (AMS) refers to the discomfort or pain experienced in muscles during physical activity or shortly after its cessation, typically lasting no longer than an hour. It is distinct from delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS), which can persist for up to 72 hours following muscle activity. Pathophysiology Acute muscle soreness is primarily attributed to microtears in muscle fibers or the surrounding fascia. This condition often arises after engaging in a new physical activity or exercise, resuming exercise after a prolonged sedentary period, or making significant changes to an existing exercise routine. The mechanisms underlying AMS include reduced oxygen availability in the muscles, increased lactic acid production, the generation of free radicals, exercise-induced rhabdomyolysis, and tissue swelling within the muscle. A newer theory suggests that AMS is caused by the accumulation of ATP-derived hydrogen ions in the muscles, leading to a decrease in pH and localized acidosis. This drop in pH is believed to be responsible for the soreness perceived by the individual. However, hydrogen ions may not be the sole contributors, as other substances capable of lowering pH and increasing acidosis could theoretically also play a role in AMS. Causes Common Causes: Physical exercise Microtears in muscle tissue Causes by Organ System: Musculoskeletal system Causes in Alphabetical Order: Exercise Influenza vaccine Muscle tears Repetitive strain injury Shin splints Strength training Stretch-shortening exercises Natural History, Complications, and Prognosis Acute muscle soreness typically resolves quickly, as implied by the term acute. To expedite recovery, it is advisable to cease the activity or movement causing the soreness. However, the discomfort may persist for up to an hour even after the cessation of muscle activity. Treatment There are several methods to accelerate recovery and alleviate the associated pain. These approaches focus on the removal of ATP-derived hydrogen ions from the muscles. Techniques that enhance the clearance of these ions can effectively shorten the recovery period. Recommended Techniques: Light aerobic exercise Stretching Massaging the affected muscles or areas
